originalTitle: Mahindra Q1 net profit rises 34%, standalone earnings beat estimates
simplifiedContent: Mahindra & Mahindra, a large company, made 34% more profit in the first quarter of the year compared to the same time last year. This increase was mainly due to strong sales of SUVs and tractors. However, the company's profit was slightly affected by higher costs of raw materials. The company's other businesses also did well, helping with the overall good results. Despite some challenges, the company still expects to meet its financial targets for the whole year.

originalTitle: US stocks: Amazon beats estimates for quarterly cloud revenue growth
simplifiedContent: Amazon just released its quarterly financial report, and it's good news: the company made more money from its cloud services than expected. This is partly because big businesses are spending more on artificial intelligence, which Amazon's cloud services support. Other big tech companies, like Microsoft and Google, also had strong cloud revenue growth, but Amazon's performance was especially impressive. This matters because it shows that Amazon's investments in artificial intelligence are paying off, which could help the company continue to grow. Amazon's online shopping business also did well, especially during its Prime Day event, which adds to the company's overall success.

originalTitle: US stocks: US market ends sharply higher, lifted by soaring Microsoft
simplifiedContent: Here's what happened in the US stock market: it had a big up day on Thursday, thanks in part to Microsoft doing better than expected. Microsoft's good news helped calm worries that spending on artificial intelligence would hurt the company. Other big tech companies like Alphabet and Meta didn't do as well because they're spending a lot on AI. The companies that make computer chips also had a good day, which helped the overall market. This matters because it shows that despite some concerns, the market is still moving forward, with some areas of strength and others of weakness.

originalTitle: Fitch’s Private Credit Default Rate Hit Record in Second Quarter
simplifiedContent: Fitch Ratings, a company that tracks debt, found that a record number of private debt borrowers in the US defaulted on their loans in the second quarter. This means that out of the 1,300 borrowers they were watching, more of them than ever before failed to pay back their debts. This is important because it shows that many borrowers are struggling to pay back their loans, which can be a sign of economic trouble. The default rate hit a record high, which is a significant change from previous quarters. This matters because it can affect the overall health of the economy and the companies that lend money.

originalTitle: Yen soars as analysts suspect official intervention; dollar broadly weaker
simplifiedContent: The value of the Japanese yen has increased suddenly, which means it can buy more of other currencies than it could before. This happened because some experts think that the Japanese government or banking officials might be secretly buying yen to make its value go up. As a result, the US dollar is now weaker compared to other currencies. This matters because it can affect international trade and investments, and might influence the prices of goods and stocks. The change in the yen's value is significant enough that it's making news in the global foreign exchange market.

originalTitle: UK’s FCA to Publish Daily Stock-Trading Data Starting Friday
simplifiedContent: The UK's main financial regulator, the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA), will start releasing daily reports on stock trading activity in the UK. This means that the FCA will share information on how many shares are being bought and sold each day. The goal of doing this is to make the stock market more transparent, which can help investors make informed decisions. The FCA will start publishing these daily reports this Friday. This change matters because it will give investors more information about what's happening in the stock market, which can help them understand what's going on with their investments.
